name: Payee assurance & Nacha fraud-monitoring controls for lower mid-market ACH/wire originators
problem: Vendor-impersonation BEC redirects outbound payments; since Jun 22 2026 every non-consumer ACH originator must run documented risk-based fraud monitoring
customer: Controllers/CFOs at US firms with ~20-1,000 employees paying vendors from ERP-generated bank files or bank portals
workaround: Email + ad-hoc callbacks, spreadsheet vendor master, bank positive pay (inbound checks only)
competitors: Trustpair, Eftsure/Sis ID/Relish (enterprise); BILL/Ramp/Stampli/Tipalti (only payments routed through them); JPM AVS/EWS (bank-side APIs); PaymentWorks, Trustmi, Nuvo
economic_loss: [F] IC3 2025 BEC reported $3.046B (floor; ~$123k per complaint [D]); [F] 60% of BEC victims cite vendor impersonation; [F] only 22% recovered >=75%
wtp: [E] $2.4k-$15k/yr for mid-market (below enterprise quotes); anchored to crime-policy sublimits $100-250k and avg incident ~$123k
market_size: [D] ~607k US firms with 20-499 employees (SUSB 2021); [E] 25-45% originate ACH/wires outside AP suites
growth: [F] B2B ACH +10% in 2025; [F] Nacha Phase 2 mandatory Jun 2026
competition: Enterprise tier crowded; lower mid-market thinly served
retention_mechanism: Vendor master of verified payees + evidence history + annual-review artefacts = switching cost
monetization: Subscription by payment volume band + per-verification usage
moat: Verified-payee network data, workflow ownership, audit evidence
why_now: Nacha Phase 2 (Jun 22 2026) + insurers conditioning social-engineering cover on documented callbacks + AI-scaled BEC
why_unsolved: Enterprise vendors sales-led and priced for large AP; AP suites only protect their own rails; before 2026 no rule forced every originator
falsifier: If ODFIs accept a one-page written policy and never ask for evidence, and firms perceive AP-suite controls as sufficient, WTP collapses
